classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish radii from diameters and calculate whole-circle, semicircle, quadrant and sector areas.

content.prompt: Find the approximate value of the area of each figure shown below. Use $\pi\approx3.14$.

spec.description: Unfilled circle with centre dot and horizontal radius labelled above. Decorative source blue and red become ordinary black.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius is visible.

spec.description: Unfilled circle with centre dot and horizontal radius labelled above. Ordinary marks use black.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius is visible.

spec.description: Circle with horizontal diameter, centre dot and full-width dimension arrow above the diameter, including endpoint extension marks.
Upper-right quadrant with vertical left radius, horizontal bottom radius and label beneath the bottom edge. No added right-angle marker.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied radius is visible.

answer.worked:
A quadrant is one-quarter of a circle.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac14\pi r^2\\A&\approx\frac14\times3.14\times3^2\\A&\approx7.065\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Upper semicircle with diameter, centre dot and full-width dimension arrow below, retaining endpoint extensions.

answer.worked:
$r=12\div2=6\text{ cm}$. A semicircle is half a circle.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\pi r^2\\A&\approx\frac12\times3.14\times6^2\\A&\approx56.52\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Left vertex with two radii extending right to the arc. Angle label lies inside near the vertex; radius label lies below the lower edge. No angle arc is added.
spec.mathematics: Sector of radius 40 mm and central angle 45 degrees.

answer.short:
$628\text{ mm}^2$

The sector is $\frac18$ of a full circle.
answer.worked:
$\frac{45}{360}=\frac18$, so the sector is one-eighth of the circle.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{45}{360}\pi r^2\\A&\approx\frac18\times3.14\times40^2\\A&\approx628\text{ mm}^2\end{align*}$$
